result:
The investigation is complete. I wrote the full enumeration to `runs/02_auth_sweep/REPORT.md` — no other files were touched.

**Key findings:**
- **63 registered routes total; 47 have no auth at all** (X-API-Key or Stripe signature) — more than double DECISIONS.md's "~20" estimate. Worth re-scoping the fix session before starting.
- **Zero routes have an explicit "intentionally public" comment anywhere in the backend** — I grepped for it. So strictly, every no-auth route is UNVERIFIED-INTENT; I grouped them by content shape (reference data / LLM cost / PII-tenancy / payment / packet-write) so the fix session can triage fast, but none are cleared as confirmed-intentional.
- **10 key-gated-but-no-ownership routes (IDOR)**, listed separately per the task's instruction not to fix them here — includes the three already named in AUDIT_FINDINGS §4.9 plus 7 more I found (`/user/{user_id}`, `push-token`, `/subscribe/{user_id}`, `/process/{session_id}`, deadline/triage analyze-by-document_id routes).
- Frontend cross-check surfaced one broken call path: `PaywallPage.jsx:23` fetches `/checkout/{documentId}`, which doesn't exist as a backend route anywhere — flagged as open/unresolved, not a security gap.
- A few forms sub-routes (`/api/forms/case-types`, `/decision-tree`, `/facets`, `/counties`, `/recommend`, `/meta/{form_number}`) had no direct frontend call site found via grep — noted as unverified rather than asserted dead, since a shared helper could call them.

Report has full file:line citations, the verified-vs-inferred-vs-open breakdown, and doesn't touch any code.
